question: Evaluate: (5^(1)/(4)) times (125⁰.²⁵)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert terms to the same prime base: 125 = 5³ and 0.25 = 1/4

⇒ 5¹/⁴ × (5³)¹/⁴

⇒ 5¹/⁴ × 5³/⁴ = 5⁽¹/⁴ ⁺ ³/⁴⁾

⇒ 5¹ = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = 5¹/⁴ × 125⁰.²⁵

**Formula Used:**

am × bm = (a × b)m

**Calculation:**

⇒ Since 1/4 = 0.25, the expression can be written as:

⇒ 5⁰.²⁵ × 125⁰.²⁵

⇒ Applying the formula am × bm = (a × b)m:

⇒ (5 × 125)⁰.²⁵

⇒ 625⁰.²⁵

⇒ Converting the decimal power back to a fraction (0.25 = 1/4):

⇒ 625¹/⁴

⇒ We know that 625 = 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 = 5⁴

⇒ (5⁴)¹/⁴

⇒ 5⁴ × ⁽¹/⁴⁾

⇒ 5¹ = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product Rule of Indices

When multiplying terms with the same base, add their exponents: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ

Power of a Power Rule

When raising a power to another power, multiply the exponents: (am)ⁿ = amⁿ

Power of a Product Rule

When multiplying terms with the same exponent, multiply their bases: am × bm = (a × b)m
